facts.text: I asked how logic helps analyze and evaluate arguments.
I asked whether people can use emotions and personal opinions to make arguments seem more convincing.
I questioned whether logic is used by people in power to control the narrative and silence diverse voices and opinions.
I expressed distrust in a system that has been used to oppress people in the past.
I said logic seems to reinforce the status quo.
I asked who gets to decide what counts as sound reasoning and valid evidence.
I said the standards for sound reasoning and valid evidence are set by those in power.
I said this sounds like theoretical mumbo-jumbo.
I said that in the real world people don't always apply logic and critical thinking.
I said emotions and biases often drive decision-making.
I asked how logic can overcome emotions and biases.
I said I still don't trust logic.
I said logic seems to create an illusion of impartiality and objectivity.
I said logic is influenced by personal biases and underlying power structures.
I said that even if logic is used to evaluate arguments, subjective judgment calls are being made.
